executive_assessment.text: Brokopondo/Sipaliwini water systems and selected sites in Para/Marowijne add concrete adaptation detail, with institutional exclusion and monitoring gaps.
Historical interior flood/road impacts and differentiated preparedness sit alongside land-rights contention. IICA results are implementer reports, not causal effects or proven peace outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-04-01 reports: In 2022, EnGenDER provided 95 water tanks to three Indigenous and 34 tribal communities in Brokopondo and Sipaliwini districts; Klaaskreek also received water-system rehabilitation.

Source dated 2025-04-01 reports: An IICA project installed low-cost rainwater systems at selected households in Matta and Singri Lanti (Para District) and Tamarin (Marowijne District) to expand potable-water storage.

Source dated 2023-06 reports: Heavy rains in March 2022 flooded Brokopondo and other interior districts; reported effects included crop losses, hunger and nearly 1,500 displaced people, while flooded southern roads challenged relief access.

known_gaps.text: No countrywide causal estimate of climate impacts on conflict or violence is established by these sources.
Full subnational coverage and independently evaluated long-term response effectiveness remain gaps.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

No inspected primary source demonstrated a climate-to-conflict causal pathway or violence/insecurity constraining adaptation delivery. Interior land-rights contention is relevant context but is not linked by the SCD to climate hazards.
The NAP progress report relies on stakeholder reporting and notes missing indicator information; its activities and outputs are not an independent impact evaluation.
The World Bank SCD draws on 2022 consultations and a 2023 phone survey, and warns that some conditions may have changed since the report was drafted.
IICA's finalized 2023-2024 project results are implementer-reported, without an independent counterfactual or quantified food-security effect.
The IICA 2025-2026 project listing was accessed after its stated end date but does not say whether planned activities were completed.
The IDB State of the Climate PDF exceeded the web reader's 10 MB limit and was not used; recent, district-disaggregated hazard and preparedness evidence remains limited.
Land-rights contention is kept as institutional context, not attributed to climate. Crop-variety recovery is adaptive capacity, not a peace outcome.
NAP report publication precision corrected to April 2025; the cover does not support a specific first-of-month day. Physical/printed page conventions remain distinct.
